claim: The mushroom body (MB) is a well-characterized associative memory structure within the Drosophila brain.
source: The mushroom body (MB) is a well-characterized associative memory structure within the Drosophila brain.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the mushroom body structure in Drosophila.

claim: Using trans-Tango, the study identified divergent projections across the brain and convergent downstream targets of the MB output neurons (MBONs).
source: Using the genetic anterograde transsynaptic tracing tool, trans-Tango, we identified divergent projections across the brain and convergent downstream targets of the MB output neurons (MBONs).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data using trans-Tango.

claim: At least three separate targets receive convergent input from MBONs: other MBONs, the fan-shaped body (FSB), and the lateral accessory lobe (LAL).
source: Our analysis revealed at least three separate targets that receive convergent input from MBONs: other MBONs, the fan-shaped body (FSB), and the lateral accessory lobe (LAL).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the analysis of trans-Tango data.

claim: Inhibitory and excitatory MBONs converge on the same genetic subset of FSB and LAL neurons.
source: We describe, both anatomically and functionally, a multilayer circuit in which inhibitory and excitatory MBONs converge on the same genetic subset of FSB and LAL neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated both anatomically and functionally in the study.

claim: This circuit architecture enables the brain to update and integrate information with previous experience before executing appropriate behavioral responses.
source: This circuit architecture enables the brain to update and integrate information with previous experience before executing appropriate behavioral responses.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the observed circuit architecture.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster has a nervous system of approximately 100,000 neurons.
source: With a nervous system of approximately 100,000 neurons and a rich genetic toolkit that offers the potential to selectively manipulate subsets of neurons in behaving animals, significant effort has been devoted to establishing a detailed map of structural neural connectivity in the fly in an effort to then layer on function (Aso et al., 2014a; Bates et al., 2020; Couto et al., 2005; Deng et al., 2019; Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Frechter et al., 2019; Grabe et al., 2015; Kondo et al., 2020; Li et al., 2020; Marin et al., 2020; Otto et al., 2020; Peng et al., 2011; Shao et al., 2014; Takemura et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila neurobiology, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Significant effort has been devoted to establishing a detailed map of structural neural connectivity in the fly.
source: With a nervous system of approximately 100,000 neurons and a rich genetic toolkit that offers the potential to selectively manipulate subsets of neurons in behaving animals, significant effort has been devoted to establishing a detailed map of structural neural connectivity in the fly in an effort to then layer on function (Aso et al., 2014a; Bates et al., 2020; Couto et al., 2005; Deng et al., 2019; Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Frechter et al., 2019; Grabe et al., 2015; Kondo et al., 2020; Li et al., 2020; Marin et al., 2020; Otto et al., 2020; Peng et al., 2011; Shao et al., 2014; Takemura et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: trans-Tango is a synthetic signaling pathway that converts the activation of a cell surface receptor into expression of a reporter gene via site-specific proteolysis.
source: In trans-Tango, a synthetic signaling pathway converts the activation of a cell surface receptor into expression of a reporter gene via site-specific proteolysis.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of trans-Tango, which is established knowledge from the cited work.

claim: trans-Tango was developed by Talay et al., 2017.
source: This pathway is introduced into all neurons while the starter neurons of interest express the ligand that activates the pathway and present it in their synapses. Binding of the ligand to its receptor on the postsynaptic partners activates the signaling pathway and leads to expression of a reporter that selectively labels these postsynaptic neurons (Talay et al., 2017).
evidence: The citation indicates that Talay et al., 2017 is the source of trans-Tango.

claim: The insect MB integrates inputs from multiple sensory modalities.
source: The insect MB is a prominent neuropil structure that integrates inputs from multiple sensory modalities (Caron et al., 2013; Ehmer and Gronenberg, 2002; Gruntman and Turner, 2013; Li and Strausfeld, 1997; Li and Strausfeld, 1999; Liu et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2016; Marin et al., 2020; Marin et al., 2002; Schildberger, 1984; Strausfeld and Li, 1999a; Strausfeld and Li, 1999b; Vogt et al., 2016; Vogt et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2016; Yagi et al., 2016; Zars, 2000)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The MB has a well-established role in learning and memory.
source: and has a well-established role in learning and memory (Davis, 1993; de Belle and Heisenberg, 1994; Heisenberg, 1998; Heisenberg, 2003; Heisenberg et al., 1985; Pascual and Préat, 2001; Zars et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The MB comprises thousands of densely packed Kenyon cell neural fibers that are organized into three separate lobes (α/β, α′/β′, and γ).
source: The MB comprises thousands of densely packed Kenyon cell neural fibers that are organized into three separate lobes (α/β, α′/β′, and γ).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about the MB structure.

claim: Kenyon cell neural fibers form en passant synapses along the length of their axons with efferent cells called MB output neurons (MBONs).
source: Kenyon cell neural fibers form en passant synapses along the length of their axons with efferent cells called MB output neurons (MBONs; Aso et al., 2014a; Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020; Li and Strausfeld, 1997; Li and Strausfeld, 1999; Mobbs, 1982; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The MB integrates valence-related input from dopamine neurons (DANs).
source: In addition to receiving processed sensory information, the MB integrates valence-related input from dopamine neurons (DANs; Aso et al., 2014a; Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The MB is positioned as a high-level integration center for the representations of multisensory cues and their perceived valence.
source: This architecture positions the MB as a high-level integration center for the representations of multisensory cues and their perceived valence.
evidence: This is an inference based on the described anatomical and functional properties of the MB.

claim: Split-Gal4 lines enabled selective genetic access to specific neuronal populations in the Drosophila MB.
source: A more refined analysis of the neural circuits associated with the Drosophila MB was recently achieved through the use of split-Gal4 lines that enabled selective genetic access to specific neuronal populations (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited work.

claim: Split-Gal4 lines delineate a compartmentalization of the MB lobes by overlapping patterns of innervating DANs and MBONs.
source: These delineate a compartmentalization of the MB lobes by overlapping patterns of innervating DANs and MBONs (Aso et al., 2014a; Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Projections from the MBONs terminate within discrete neuropils, including the lateral horn (LH), crepine (CRE), superior medial (SMP), intermediate (SIP), and lateral (SLP) protocerebrum.
source: Projections from the MBONs terminate within discrete neuropils, including the lateral horn (LH), crepine (CRE), superior medial (SMP), intermediate (SIP), and lateral (SLP) protocerebrum (Aso et al., 2014a; Ito et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: These neuropils have been described as convergence sites of MBONs as different MBONs send converging outputs to similar subregions in these structures.
source: These neuropils have also been described as convergence sites of MBONs as different MBONs send converging outputs to similar subregions in these structures (Aso et al., 2014a; Ito et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Evidence suggests that MBON axons synapse onto dendrites of DANs and other MBONs providing opportunities for feedback to the MB.
source: Within these neuropils, evidence suggests that MBON axons synapse onto dendrites of DANs and other MBONs providing opportunities for feedback to the MB (Aso et al., 2014a; Eichler et al., 2017; Scaplen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Evidence suggests MBON axons synapse onto dendrites of neurons projecting to other structures, including the FSB.
source: Evidence also suggests MBON axons synapse onto dendrites of neurons projecting to other structures, including the FSB (Aso et al., 2014a; Eichler et al., 2017; Scaplen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MBONs in the adult brain are hypothesized to synapse on local interneurons whose processes are confined to the limits of the target neuropil.
source: Additionally, similar to other insects and to the first instar Drosophila larva, MBONs in the adult brain are hypothesized to synapse on local interneurons whose processes are confined to the limits of the target neuropil but play a role in modulating input and output signals (Eichler et al., 2017; Phillips-Portillo and Strausfeld, 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: The study successfully identified the postsynaptic connections of 25 split-GAL4 lines.
source: We successfully identified the postsynaptic connections of 25 split-GAL4 lines (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–23, open access raw data video files are available at https://doi.org/10.26300/mttr-r782).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: trans-Tango signals from MB112C (MBON γ1pedc>α/β) and G0239 (MBON α3) were too weak and were excluded from further analysis.
source: trans-Tango signals from MB112C (MBON γ1pedc>α/β) and G0239 (MBON α3) were too weak and were excluded from further analysis.
evidence: This describes a methodological limitation in the study.

claim: Signals from MB242A (MBON calyx) proved to be too noisy to confidently identify postsynaptic connections.
source: In contrast, signals from MB242A (MBON calyx) proved to be too noisy to confidently identify postsynaptic connections.
evidence: This describes a methodological limitation in the study.

claim: Postsynaptic connections of glutamatergic, GABAergic, and cholinergic MBONs vary with regard to the divergence and breadth of their postsynaptic connections.
source: Postsynaptic connections of glutamatergic, GABAergic, and cholinergic MBONs vary with regard to the divergence and breadth of their postsynaptic connections (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–23, external open access raw data video files are available at https://doi.org/10.26300/mttr-r782).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data and figures.

claim: MB011B, which includes glutamatergic MBONs γ5β′2a, β′2mp, and β′2mp-bilateral has extensive connections across the superior protocerebrum.
source: For instance, MB011B, which includes glutamatergic MBONs γ5β′2a, β′2mp, and β′2mp-bilateral has extensive connections across the superior protocerebrum (Figure 1A)
evidence: This is a specific observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: MB542B, which includes cholinergic MBONs α′1, α2p3p, α′3 m has limited connections within the LH.
source: whereas MB542B, which includes cholinergic MBONs α′1, α2p3p, α′3 m has limited connections within the LH (Figure 1N).
evidence: This is a specific observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 1N.

claim: The innervation patterns did not seem to correlate with neurotransmitter type or number of MBONs expressing each split-GAL4.
source: The innervation patterns did not seem to correlate with neurotransmitter type or number of MBONs expressing each split-GAL4.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Of the DANs innervating the MB, 90% have dendritic arborizations that are localized to four of the five proposed MBON convergent regions, including CRE, SMP, SIP, and SLP.
source: Of the DANs innervating the MB, 90% have dendritic arborizations that are localized to four of the five proposed MBON convergent regions, including CRE, SMP, SIP, and SLP (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited work.

claim: Some of the neurons postsynaptic to MBONs were TH positive.
source: As expected, some of the neurons postsynaptic to MBONs were TH positive
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data using TH staining.

source: Most overlap between TH and trans-Tango signals was observed with γ5β′2a (MB011B, 25 ± 0.7; n = 4; Figure 3A) and β′2mp (MB002B, 10.25 ± 1.3 n = 4 and MB074C, 4.75 ± 1.1, n = 4; Figure 3B and C) MBONs.

source: Similarly, the γ3, γ3β′1 MBON was predicted to overlap with PAM γ3 and β′1m
evidence: This is a prediction from previous work.

source: and MB083C had an average of nine cells (9 ± 2.0, n = 10) with co-expression of TH and trans-Tango signals (Figure 3D).

claim: The cholinergic γ2α′1 MBON (MB077C) was predicted to overlap with PAM γ4>γ1γ2.
source: Likewise, the cholinergic γ2α′1 MBON (MB077C) was predicted to overlap with PAM γ4>γ1γ2
evidence: This is a prediction from previous work.

source: and indeed, MB077C brains averaged five cells (5 ± 1.5, n = 8) with co-expression of TH and trans-Tango signals per hemibrain (Figure 3E).

claim: Nearly all MBONs have divergent connections across the dorsal brain regions, CRE, SMP, SIP, SLP, LH, as well as FSB, and LAL.
source: Nearly all MBONs have divergent connections across the dorsal brain regions, CRE, SMP, SIP, SLP, LH, as well as FSB, and LAL (Figure 2C–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

source: MBON γ1pedc>α/β have dendritic arbors in γ1 and axonal projections in α/β lobes

source: and MBON β1>α has dendritic arbors in β1 and axon projections to the entire alpha lobe.

source: Two different MBONs are frequently targeted: MBON β′2mp (Figure 4A) and MBON γ3β′1 (Figure 4B).

source: Interestingly, MBON β′2mp receives convergent glutamatergic, GABAergic, and cholinergic input from MBON γ5β′2a (MB011B and MB210B), MBON γ3β′1 (MB110C and MB83C), MBON α′2 (MB018B and MB082C), and MBON γ2α′1 (MB077B and MB051C) (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

source: MBON γ3β′1 receives convergent input from glutamatergic MBON β′2mp as revealed with split-GAL4 lines MB002B (Figure 4B) and MB074C (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and glutamatergic MBON γ4>γ1γ2 (MB298B, Figure 4B).

claim: MBON γ3β′1 and MBON β′2mp create opportunities for multilevel feedforward networks to update information to drive behavioral response.
source: We hypothesize that similar to MBONs that project to other regions of the MB, MBON γ3β′1, and MBON β′2mp create opportunities for multilevel feedforward networks to update information to drive behavioral response (Figure 4C).

source: For instance, trans-Tango with MBON γ2α′1 consistently visualized projections to FSB layers 4 and 5 in all the brains analyzed

source: whereas more variability was observed in FSB innervation pattern across MBON α′2 brains (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).

source: MBON α′1 and α2sc both project exclusively to FSB layer 6 (Figure 5C).

claim: Cholinergic MBON γ2α′1 consistently had postsynaptic neurites within the LAL.

claim: Neurons innervating the LAL receive convergent input from combinations of glutamatergic, GABAergic and cholinergic MBONs.
source: Thus, like the FSB, neurons innervating the LAL receives convergent input from combinations of glutamatergic, GABAergic and cholinergic MBONs (Figure 6D; Figure 6E).
